exercise.name: Cable Concentration Extension (on knee)

reference.title: Cable Concentration Extension (on knee)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching: half-kneeling facing a pulley set at about head height, working upper arm braced on the inside of the front thigh)

equipment: Cable machine (pulley at about head height)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you push the handle down, breathe in as it rises.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s down, short pause, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can push down with the working elbow still at your side for every rep.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; slower return. Do the same reps with each arm.

cues.text: Kneel on the left knee facing a pulley set at about head height, right foot forward. Lean forward from the hips and brace the back of the right upper arm against the inside of the right thigh; take the D-handle underhand, elbow well bent, left hand on the hip.
Breathe out and straighten the elbow, pushing the handle down until the arm hangs straight; the upper arm stays on the thigh.
Squeeze the back of the arm for a moment, wrist straight.
Breathe in and let the handle rise slowly until the elbow is well bent again.
Brief pause with the cable taut, then repeat; switch arms (and kneeling legs) after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the upper arm off the thigh
mistakes.fix: Keep the arm braced; only the forearm moves.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back over the knee
mistakes.fix: Hinge from the hips with a long back.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the handle yank the elbow shut
mistakes.fix: Control the return over about 2 s.
Keep the wrist in line with the forearm.

kinematics.norm: From well bent to straight (clinical opinion)
Braced on the inside of the front thigh and still, hanging close to vertical; with the arm near the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018)
Underhand (palm toward the fold of the elbow) on a D-handle (clinical opinion)
Half-kneeling, leaning forward from the hips with a long back (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Concentration Extension (on knee), video (movement reference)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)

Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position (Eur J Sport Sci 2022, DOI 10.1080/17461391.2022.2100279; PubMed 35819335; 21 adults, 12 weeks, cable)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain in the elbow, shoulder or kneeling knee, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with the upper arm braced.
Put a pad or folded mat under the kneeling knee.
Keep the head out of the cable's path: set the pulley so the cable runs in front of the face.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee discomfort: sit on a bench with the arm braced on the thigh instead.
Elbow pain: lighter load and a shorter range (clinical opinion).
progressions: Pause 1-2 s with the arm straight.
Overhead cable triceps extension (more triceps growth than the arm-at-the-side position in a 12-week study, PubMed 35819335).

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the cable, one arm at a time. With the upper arm at the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018); training in this position gave less triceps growth than overhead extensions in a 12-week study (PubMed 35819335).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Prime mover: straightens the elbow against the cable, one arm at a time. With the upper arm at the side the long head carried the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018); training in this position gave less triceps growth than overhead extensions in a 12-week study (PubMed 35819335).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keeps the upper arm pressed against the thigh.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keeps the upper arm pressed against the thigh.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Keeps the upper arm from drifting forward.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Keeps the upper arm from drifting forward.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still and square so body weight does not push the handle.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Keep the trunk from twisting toward the working arm.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Keep the trunk from twisting toward the working arm.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the long back in the forward lean.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the long back in the forward lean.

guides.label: Forearm swings down, upper arm braced
